raw_graphql_pull_request.body: This PR was originally stacked on #30947, which is now merged. ## Motivation After draft-extend CUDA graph replay, the top-k=1 decode path still materializes selected logits, hidden states, and optional DSA indices with eager indexing, then launches `argmax` and `ones_like`. For wide vocabularies, these small eager launches form a visible tail after the graph and unnecessarily materialize the selected full-vocabulary logits. The draft-extend path needs the same split argmax reduction introduced by #30947, with one difference: it reduces selected rows from a larger logits tensor. This PR extends that implementation instead of adding a second draft-extend reduction kernel. cc @kpham-sgl ## Modification - Reuse #30947's `_draft_topk1_partial_argmax_kernel` for both paths. A compile-time `USE_ROW_INDICES` specialization either loads the selected source row for draft-extend or compiles the row-indexing branch away for regular draft. - Reuse a common `_draft_topk1_finalize` helper for the second-stage reduction. - Replace separate `tl.max` and `tl.argmax` partial reductions with one `tl.max(..., return_indices=True)` reduction. This also improves the already-merged #30947 regular-draft path. - Fuse final argmax assembly, `topk_p = 1`, hidden-state gathering, and optional DSA-index gathering into the draft-extend final Triton launch. - Overlay hidden-state and DSA gathering on the same task grid, using `max(hidden_blocks, dsa_blocks)` gather tasks rather than separate task ranges. - Replace three eager indexed gathers plus `argmax` and `ones_like` with two Triton launches. - Enable the path only for CUDA, `topk == 1`, and non-rejection sampling; preserve the existing fallback for other modes and backends. - Add focused exactness coverage at the traced GLM dimensions and CUDA graph benchmarks for both the new path and the inherited #30947 path. ## Accuracy GLM5.2-FP8 B300, eval unchanged from main: ```bash == gsm8k == 1319 examples (single-shot) | 552.4s | 1968 tok/s | 1.1M tokens * score = 94.39% stop_rate = 96.36% truncated_rate = 3.64% [warn: hitting max_tokens] error_rate = 0.00% ``` ## Speedup All microbenchmarks use CUDA graph replay (`triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph`) on an idle NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC GPU with CUDA 13.0. ### Draft-extend postprocess Fused draft-extend path versus the eager indexed-gather reference. The benchmark uses FP32 logits shaped `[6 * batch_size, 154880]`, BF16 hidden states of width 6144, and INT32 DSA top-k indices of width 2048. | Batch size | Fused indexed Triton | Eager index + argmax | Speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 3.84 us | 24.52 us | 6.39x | | 2 | 3.84 us | 17.50 us | 4.56x | | 4 | 4.04 us | 18.10 us | 4.48x | | 8 | 4.18 us | 18.45 us | 4.41x | | 16 | 4.91 us | 21.97 us | 4.47x | | 32 | 5.71 us | 26.59 us | 4.66x | | 64 | 8.29 us | 39.36 us | 4.75x | | 128 | 13.89 us | 71.46 us | 5.14x | ### Impact on the #30947 kernel The table below runs #30947's original CUDA graph benchmark at the GLM5.2 vocabulary size (151552), comparing the implementation merged in main (`6c042aeb1`) with this PR (`e8ca6f423`). Lower is better. | Workload | Batch size | Merged #30947 | This PR | Latency reduction | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Draft postprocess | 1 | 3.881 us | 3.736 us | 3.7% | | Draft postprocess | 16 | 4.933 us | 4.667 us | 5.4% | | Draft postprocess | 128 | 12.340 us | 11.328 us | 8.2% | | Draft postprocess | 2048 | 199.201 us | 178.823 us | 10.2% | | Chain materialize | 1 | 8.241 us | 7.934 us | 3.7% | | Chain materialize | 16 | 11.243 us | 10.720 us | 4.7% | | Chain materialize | 128 | 37.957 us | 36.228 us | 4.6% | | Chain materialize | 2048 | 400.914 us | 362.974 us | 9.5% | Across both tested vocabulary sizes (129280 and 151552) and all 12 batch sizes, this PR was faster at all 24 points in each report. Mean latency reduction was 5.1% for draft postprocess and 4.5% for chain materialization. main: PR: --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #30799939556](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30799939556) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #30799939191](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30799939191)

Thanks @mattteochen. Closing this because you have 16 PRs open and none updated in 7 days, over our soft cap of 5 for idle PRs.

Reopen the two or three you most want reviewed - a short active set moves faster than a long idle one.

Some directories moved recently, so an older branch may need retargeting:
`sgl-kernel/` -> `python/sglang/kernels/aot/`, `python/sglang/jit_kernel/`
-> `python/sglang/kernels/jit/`, `docs/` -> `docs/docs/` (`.mdx`),
`bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces optimized Triton kernels for topk=1 speculative decoding postprocessing, specifically `draft_topk1_postprocess` and `draft_extend_topk1_postprocess`. These kernels fuse argmax reduction, position advancement, and draft token writing to bypass slower eager PyTorch operations during speculative steps. The changes integrate these kernels into the Eagle speculative worker (`eagle_worker_v2.py`) and add comprehensive unit tests and benchmarks to verify correctness and performance. There are no review comments, so I have no feedback to provide.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The [consumer version of Gemini Code Assist on GitHub](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-repo-code) is being sunset. Starting **June 18, 2026**, new organization installations will be blocked, and all code review activity will officially cease on **July 17, 2026**.
> For more details on the timeline and next steps, please review the [Help Documentation](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/deprecations/consumer-code-review).

 import triton.language as tl
 
 _DRAFT_TOPK1_BLOCK = 8192
+_DRAFT_TOPK1_GATHER_BLOCK = 1024
 
 
 @triton.jit
 def _draft_topk1_partial_argmax_kernel(
     logits,
     partial_vals,
     partial_indices,
+    row_indices,
     logits_row_stride,
     vocab_size: tl.constexpr,
     num_splits: tl.constexpr,
+    USE_ROW_INDICES: tl.constexpr,
     BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
 ):
     # int64 row base: row * stride overflows int32 once bs * vocab reaches 2^31.
-    row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    out_row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    src_row = (
+        tl.load(row_indices + out_row).to(tl.int64) if USE_ROW_INDICES else out_row
+    )
     split = tl.program_id(1)
     offsets = split * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
     mask = offsets < vocab_size
     vals = tl.load(
-        logits + row * logits_row_stride + offsets,
+        logits + src_row * logits_row_stride + offsets,
         mask=mask,
         other=-float("inf"),
     ).to(tl.float32)
     # Keep NaNs on valid lanes from selecting the masked tail.
     vals = tl.where(vals == vals, vals, -1e30)
 
-    max_val = tl.max(vals, axis=0)
-    local_index = tl.argmax(vals, axis=0)
-    out_offset = row * num_splits + split
+    max_val, local_index = tl.max(vals, axis=0, return_indices=True)
+    out_offset = out_row * num_splits + split
     tl.store(partial_vals + out_offset, max_val)
     tl.store(partial_indices + out_offset, split * BLOCK + local_index)
 
 
+@triton.jit
+def _draft_topk1_finalize(
+    partial_vals,
+    partial_indices,
+    row,
+    num_splits: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    offsets = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = offsets < num_splits
+    vals = tl.load(
+        partial_vals + row * num_splits + offsets,
+        mask=mask,
+        other=-float("inf"),
+    )
+    split = tl.argmax(vals, axis=0)
+    return tl.load(partial_indices + row * num_splits + split).to(tl.int64)
+

+@triton.jit
+def _draft_extend_topk1_finalize_kernel(
+    partial_vals,
+    partial_indices,
+    topk_p,
+    topk_index,
+    row_indices,
+    hidden_states,
+    selected_hidden_states,
+    hidden_states_row_stride,
+    dsa_topk_indices,
+    selected_dsa_topk_indices,
+    dsa_topk_indices_row_stride,
+    num_splits: tl.constexpr,
+    hidden_size: tl.constexpr,
+    dsa_topk_size: tl.constexpr,
+    HAS_HIDDEN: tl.constexpr,
+    HAS_DSA: tl.constexpr,
+    REDUCE_BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+    GATHER_BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    task = tl.program_id(1)
+
+    if task == 0:
+        index = _draft_topk1_finalize(
+            partial_vals,
+            partial_indices,
+            row,
+            num_splits,
+            REDUCE_BLOCK,
+        )
+        tl.store(topk_index + row, index)
+        tl.store(topk_p + row, 1.0)
+    else:
+        src_row = tl.load(row_indices + row).to(tl.int64)
+        offsets = (task - 1) * GATHER_BLOCK + tl.arange(0, GATHER_BLOCK)

+        if HAS_HIDDEN:

+        if HAS_DSA:

+                dsa_topk_indices + src_row * dsa_topk_indices_row_stride + offsets,
+                mask=dsa_mask,
+                other=0,
+            )
+            tl.store(
+                selected_dsa_topk_indices + row * dsa_topk_size + offsets,
+                dsa_topk,
+                mask=dsa_mask,
+            )
+
+
+def _validate_logits(logits: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+    assert logits.ndim == 2
+    assert logits.stride(1) == 1
+    assert logits.shape[1] > 0
+
+
+def _validate_row_indices(
+    row_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    logits: torch.Tensor,
+) -> None:
+    assert row_indices.ndim == 1
+    assert row_indices.dtype == torch.long
+    assert row_indices.is_contiguous()
+    assert row_indices.device == logits.device
+
+
+def _validate_row_buffer(
+    buffer: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    name: str,
+    logits: torch.Tensor,
+) -> None:
+    assert buffer.ndim == 2, f"{name} must be two-dimensional"
+    assert buffer.stride(1) == 1, f"{name} rows must be contiguous"
+    assert buffer.shape[0] >= logits.shape[0]
+    assert buffer.device == logits.device
+
+
+def _empty_selected_rows(buffer: torch.Tensor | None, bs: int) -> torch.Tensor | None:
+    if buffer is None:
+        return None
+    return buffer.new_empty((bs, buffer.shape[1]))
+
+
+def _launch_draft_topk1_partials(
+    next_token_logits: torch.Tensor,
+    row_indices: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> tuple[int, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    use_row_indices = row_indices is not None
+    bs = row_indices.shape[0] if use_row_indices else next_token_logits.shape[0]
+    vocab_size = next_token_logits.shape[1]
+    num_splits = triton.cdiv(vocab_size, _DRAFT_TOPK1_BLOCK)
+    partial_vals = torch.empty(
+        (bs, num_splits), dtype=torch.float32, device=next_token_logits.device
+    )
+    partial_indices = torch.empty(
+        (bs, num_splits), dtype=torch.int32, device=next_token_logits.device
+    )
+    # Triton's launcher still needs a valid pointer for the disabled index mode.
+    row_indices_arg = row_indices if use_row_indices else next_token_logits
+    _draft_topk1_partial_argmax_kernel[(bs, num_splits)](
+        next_token_logits,
+        partial_vals,
+        partial_indices,
+        row_indices_arg,
+        next_token_logits.stride(0),
+        vocab_size,
+        num_splits,
+        USE_ROW_INDICES=use_row_indices,
+        BLOCK=_DRAFT_TOPK1_BLOCK,
+        num_warps=8,
+    )
+    return num_splits, partial_vals, partial_indices
+
+

     positions: torch.Tensor,

+def draft_extend_topk1_postprocess(
+    next_token_logits: torch.Tensor,
+    row_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor | None,
+    dsa_topk_indices: torch.Tensor | None,
+) -> tuple[
+    torch.Tensor,
+    torch.Tensor,
+    torch.Tensor | None,
+    torch.Tensor | None,
+]:
+    """Select and postprocess the final draft-extend row for each request.
+
+    The indexed logits rows are reduced directly, without materializing a
+    selected-logits tensor. The final reduction launch also gathers the matching
+    hidden-state and optional DSA rows. ``row_indices`` must be contiguous int64
+    and contain valid, nonnegative logits row indices.
+    """
+    _validate_logits(next_token_logits)
+    _validate_row_indices(row_indices, logits=next_token_logits)
+    if hidden_states is not None:
+        _validate_row_buffer(
+            hidden_states, name="hidden_states", logits=next_token_logits
+        )
+    if dsa_topk_indices is not None:
+        _validate_row_buffer(
+            dsa_topk_indices, name="dsa_topk_indices", logits=next_token_logits
+        )
+
+    bs = row_indices.shape[0]
+    topk_p = torch.empty((bs, 1), dtype=torch.float32, device=next_token_logits.device)
+    topk_index = torch.empty(
+        (bs, 1), dtype=torch.int64, device=next_token_logits.device
+    )
+    selected_hidden_states = _empty_selected_rows(hidden_states, bs)
+    selected_dsa_topk_indices = _empty_selected_rows(dsa_topk_indices, bs)
+    if bs == 0:
+        return (
+            topk_p,
+            topk_index,
+            selected_hidden_states,
+            selected_dsa_topk_indices,
+        )
+
+    num_splits, partial_vals, partial_indices = _launch_draft_topk1_partials(
+        next_token_logits, row_indices
+    )
+    hidden_size = hidden_states.shape[1] if hidden_states is not None else 0
+    dsa_topk_size = dsa_topk_indices.shape[1] if dsa_topk_indices is not None else 0
+    num_gather_blocks = max(
+        triton.cdiv(hidden_size, _DRAFT_TOPK1_GATHER_BLOCK),
+        triton.cdiv(dsa_topk_size, _DRAFT_TOPK1_GATHER_BLOCK),
+    )
+
+    # Disabled slots still need valid pointers for Triton's launcher.
+    hidden_states_arg = hidden_states if hidden_size else next_token_logits
+    selected_hidden_states_arg = selected_hidden_states if hidden_size else topk_p
+    dsa_topk_indices_arg = dsa_topk_indices if dsa_topk_size else partial_indices
+    selected_dsa_topk_indices_arg = (
+        selected_dsa_topk_indices if dsa_topk_size else partial_indices
+    )
+    _draft_extend_topk1_finalize_kernel[(bs, 1 + num_gather_blocks)](
+        partial_vals,
+        partial_indices,
+        topk_p,
+        topk_index,
+        row_indices,
+        hidden_states_arg,

## Code Review

This pull request introduces optimized Triton kernels for topk=1 speculative decoding postprocessing, specifically `draft_topk1_postprocess` and `draft_extend_topk1_postprocess`. These kernels fuse argmax reduction, position advancement, and draft token writing to bypass slower eager PyTorch operations during speculative steps. The changes integrate these kernels into the Eagle speculative worker (`eagle_worker_v2.py`) and add comprehensive unit tests and benchmarks to verify correctness and performance. There are no review comments, so I have no feedback to provide.
